title: [Bug]: Gemini/Vertex Realtime silently drops client tools and instructions with eager setup

judge.reasoning:
Both patches satisfy the issue's stated expected behaviour: under default eager setup a client session.update that cannot be applied now yields a client-visible invalid_request_error, and no second setup is sent. The independent tests confirm this for both on gemini and vertex_ai (all six fail on base, pass on A and B).

Patch B does exactly the ask with a small, legible change: a new provider hook `unapplied_session_update_error` on the base realtime config, a Gemini/Vertex implementation that returns an explanatory message only when setup was eagerly sent (and None under deferred setup or before any setup), and a single relay branch that emits the error when a session.update produced no backend frame. The message names `LITELLM_GEMINI_LIVE_DEFER_SETUP=true` as the supported initialization path, as the issue requested. Its tests exercise the real Gemini and Vertex configs through `client_ack_messages`, assert zero backend sends plus one error event under eager setup, and assert the deferred path still builds the setup with systemInstruction and the tool with no error. Those tests would fail before and pass after.

Patch A delivers the error too, but as part of a sweeping redesign the issue explicitly said should be agreed upstream rather than imposed: it stops sending the Gemini/Vertex setup at connect, holds and deep-merges session.updates until first content, buffers conversation items with a grace timer, adds a 240s lazy-setup deadline with a monotonic clock and ensure_future/cancel plumbing, changes `_backend_refused_session` semantics, rewrites manual-VAD activityStart/activityEnd handling, adds a Gemini voice allow-list and modality rejections gated on drop_params, threads drop_params through ProviderConfigManager and Vertex, alters existing tests' expectations (27 removed lines, renamed deferred-setup test with changed behaviour), and even edits the dashboard playground to switch turn_detection from null to server_vad. Most of this is unrelated to the reported silent drop, and it changes default runtime behaviour for every Gemini/Vertex realtime session (setup timing, item buffering latency, voice acceptance). That is substantial regression risk and it buries the actual fix. Applying the client's configuration is arguably a deeper fix, but the issue asked for an error and a separate, agreed-upon per-connection opt-in, not a replacement of the default initialization model.

On correctness both resolve the reported problem; on tests both are adequate with B's more focused; on scope A adds considerable risk and obscures the fix while B is precise; on craft B is consistent with surrounding conventions (small provider hook, existing `realtime_error_event`). B is the better fix for this issue.

issue_md:
### Description

With the default eager setup behavior, a Gemini Live voice session can connect and exchange audio while the client's initial `session.update` instructions and tools are discarded. The client receives no error explaining that its configuration was not applied

`async_realtime` sends the provider setup before starting the bidirectional relay. When the client sends `session.update`, the Gemini transformer sees that setup has already been sent and returns an empty list. Dropping a second setup avoids a provider disconnect, but it also silently loses the client's first configuration request

The normal path emits only a debug log. A later session.update with turn_detection.create_response set false now logs a warning, and every other dropped update stays at debug. The client still receives no error. A caller can therefore believe its instructions and functions are active when they are absent from the provider session

### Config

The affected path is the OpenAI-compatible realtime WebSocket adapter for Gemini/Vertex Live, with `LITELLM_GEMINI_LIVE_DEFER_SETUP` unset or false. The adapter-only reproduction below needs no provider credentials or network access

The documented workaround is `LITELLM_GEMINI_LIVE_DEFER_SETUP=true`. That makes the first client `session.update` supply the initial provider setup. This report acknowledges that existing capability and concerns silent configuration loss under the default behavior

### LiteLLM Version

Reproduced locally in a downstream build based on 1.107.0. The relevant behavior was also checked in upstream main at `18831b818c596f8b46091681cc2db65495799d52`. A pristine upstream proxy has not been exercised end to end for this report

### Steps to Repro

Run this against a checkout containing the current Gemini realtime adapter

```python
import json
import litellm
from litellm.llms.gemini.realtime.transformation import GeminiRealtimeConfig

config = GeminiRealtimeConfig()
model = "gemini-3.8-live"
event = json.dumps({
    "type": "session.update",
    "session": {
        "instructions": "Use lookup_order for order questions.",
        "tools": [{
            "type": "function",
            "name": "lookup_order",
            "description": "Look up an order",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"order_id": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["order_id"],
            },
        }],
    },
})

for deferred in (False, True):
    litellm.gemini_live_defer_setup = deferred
    initial_setup = (
        config.session_configuration_request(model)
        if config.requires_session_configuration()
        else None
    )
    forwarded = config.transform_realtime_request(event, model, initial_setup)
    print(deferred, len(forwarded))
    if forwarded:
        setup = json.loads(forwarded[0])["setup"]
        print(setup["systemInstruction"])
        print(setup["tools"][0]["function_declarations"][0]["name"])
```

Observed output

```text
False 0
True 1
{'role': 'user', 'parts': [{'text': 'Use lookup_order for order questions.'}]}
lookup_order
```

At the WebSocket level, connect with default settings, then send the same `session.update` with tools and instructions. The eager provider setup has already consumed the single setup opportunity, so that client configuration is dropped

Expected behavior is a client-visible error explaining that the update cannot be applied and identifying deferred setup as the supported initialization path. The gateway should not send a second provider setup or claim that a dropped configuration was applied

A related enhancement would allow deferred setup to be selected per connection or deployment, so gateways serving clients with different initialization behavior do not need one process-wide setting. A downstream patch currently uses an explicit per-connection opt-in and preserves the existing default for other clients. The public parameter and behavior should be agreed upstream

### References

[Documented deferred setup setting](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/config_settings)

[Gemini session update handling](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/18831b818c596f8b46091681cc2db65495799d52/litellm/llms/gemini/realtime/transformation.py)

[Realtime relay initialization](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/18831b818c596f8b46091681cc2db65495799d52/litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py)

[Related discussion about older Vertex realtime versions](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/discussions/38250)

### Which part of LiteLLM is this about?

LLM translation, Gemini and Vertex realtime session initialization

### How are you deploying?

Docker

+    def level(node, depth: int):

+class _ScriptedRealtimeBackend:
+    """Backend socket that answers the first setup frame with the scripted replies
+    and closes once the client is done, so both bridge loops run to completion."""
+
+    def __init__(self, replies_after_setup):
+        self.sent = []
+        self.closed = asyncio.Event()
+        self._replies_after_setup = list(replies_after_setup)
+        self._inbox = asyncio.Queue()
+
+    async def __aenter__(self):
+        return self
+
+    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
+        return None
+
+    async def send(self, payload):
+        self.sent.append(payload)
+        if "setup" in json.loads(payload):
+            for reply in self._replies_after_setup:
+                self._inbox.put_nowait(reply)
+
+    def close_after_replies(self):
+        self._inbox.put_nowait(None)
+
+    async def recv(self, decode=True):
+        reply = await self._inbox.get()
+        if reply is None:
+            self.closed.set()
+            raise websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK(None, None)
+        return reply
+
+
+class _ScriptedRealtimeClient:
+    def __init__(self, messages, backend):
+        self.scope = {"headers": []}
+        self.exceptions = websockets.exceptions
+        self.sent = []
+        self._messages = list(messages)
+        self._backend = backend
+
+    async def send_text(self, payload):
+        self.sent.append(payload)
+
+    async def receive_text(self):
+        if self._messages:
+            return self._messages.pop(0)
+        self._backend.close_after_replies()
+        await self._backend.closed.wait()
+        raise websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK(None, None)
+
+    async def close(self, code=None, reason=None):
+        return None
+

title: [Bug]: /tag/update 500s "BudgetNewRequest() got multiple values for keyword argument 'budget_id'" on any tag that has a budget

judge.reasoning: Both patches apply the identical root-cause fix the issue suggests: drop budget_id from the LiteLLM_BudgetTable field set so it is no longer copied into _budget_data and collides with the explicit budget_id kwarg in the existing-budget branch. Independent tests confirm both resolve every scenario, including the access-group path. The difference is in the follow-through. Patch B also changes the update branch so that when a different budget_id is sent alongside budget settings, those settings are written to the budget the entity is being re-pointed at rather than to the budget it is leaving. With Patch A, that combination (previously unreachable because it 500'd) would mutate the old budget and then re-point, which silently edits a budget the tag no longer uses; the issue's expectation that a different budget_id re-points the tag makes B's semantics the coherent one, and since the path never worked before there is no regression risk for existing callers. On tests, B is stronger: it covers the helper for same/different budget_id, exercises /tag/update end-to-end with a four-case parametrization asserting both the tag-row re-point and which budget row receives the settings, and adds two access-group tests for the second affected endpoint the issue calls out. Patch A adds one helper unit test and an integration test that depends on a tests/integration/_support/client module whose existence cannot be confirmed from the diff, and does not cover the re-point or access-group cases. Scope-wise B's extra behavioral change is small, well-commented, and tested, so it does not obscure the fix. B wins on tests and on handling the edge the issue's expected behavior implies.

issue_md:
### Description

Please note this has been found and written up by AI but hand checked by the author before sharing.

### Description

**What happens**
`POST /tag/update` returns 500 whenever the request carries `budget_id` and the tag already has a budget, even when it is the tag's own budget id, unchanged. Nothing is updated:

```
500 {"detail":"litellm.proxy._types.BudgetNewRequest() got multiple values for keyword argument 'budget_id'"}
```

The Terraform provider's `litellm_tag` sends `budget_id` on every update once it is in state, so a `litellm_tag` with `budget_id = litellm_budget.x.budget_id` can't be updated at all, whichever field changed. (A tag with no budget updates fine.)

**Root cause** (v1.105.1; unchanged on `main` today)
`handle_budget_for_entity` (`litellm/proxy/management_helpers/utils.py`) collects the request's budget fields by iterating `LiteLLM_BudgetTable.model_fields` (`utils.py:211-222`). `LiteLLM_BudgetTable` declares `budget_id` (`litellm/models/budget.py:24`), so a request that sends `budget_id` puts it in `_budget_data`, and the "existing budget" branch then calls

```python
BudgetNewRequest(budget_id=existing_budget_id, **_budget_data)   # utils.py:255
```

which raises `TypeError`. `update_tag`'s `except Exception` (`tag_management_endpoints.py:481-483`) turns it into the 500. A side effect is that lines 259-261 ("a different budget_id is explicitly provided, use that instead") can never run for a tag that already has a budget, so a tag can't be moved to another budget either.

**Expected**
`/tag/update` with the tag's current `budget_id` (plus any other fields) succeeds. With a different `budget_id`, the tag is re-pointed to that budget.

**Suggested fix**
In `handle_budget_for_entity` (`litellm/proxy/management_helpers/utils.py:180`), the request's `budget_id` is read twice:

1. **as a budget setting:** `budget_params` (`:211`) is every field of `LiteLLM_BudgetTable`, which includes `budget_id`, so the request's `budget_id` is copied into `_budget_data` (`:214-222`) alongside `max_budget`, `tpm_limit` and the rest;
2. **as "which budget this tag should point at":** `data_budget_id = getattr(data, "budget_id", None)` (`:225`). The create branch returns it (`:228-230`), and the update branch re-points the tag when it differs from the current one (`:260-261`).

Only the second is wanted. The first is what breaks `BudgetNewRequest(budget_id=existing_budget_id, **_budget_data)` (`:255`). So exclude `budget_id` from `budget_params`, and leave the `data_budget_id` handling to do its job:

```diff
-    budget_params: Final = LiteLLM_BudgetTable.model_fields.keys()
+    # budget_id selects the budget (data_budget_id below); it is not a budget setting
+    budget_params: Final = LiteLLM_BudgetTable.model_fields.keys() - {"budget_id"}
```

With that change, step 2 of the repro updates the description and keeps the budget. A `budget_id` that names a different budget re-points the tag (`:260-261`) instead of 500ing.

**Related, from the same helper (please confirm which is intended)**
- **Licence gating depends on whether the tag already has a budget.** When there is no budget yet, the helper writes the row directly (`utils.py:234-243`) without `validate_model_max_budget` (`key_management_endpoints.py:7809`, which holds the Enterprise check and the shape validation). When a budget exists, the update goes through `update_budget`, which does call it (`budget_management_endpoints.py:168-176`). So without a licence, `model_max_budget` is accepted, unvalidated, by `/tag/new` and by `/tag/update` on a tag with no budget. It is refused ("You must have an enterprise license to set model_max_budget") by `/tag/update` once the tag has a budget, and by `/budget/new` and `/budget/update`. A tag created with `model_max_budget` therefore can't have it changed later without a licence.
- `PUT /access_group/{access_group}/budget` uses the same helper (`model_access_group_management_endpoints.py:1173`), and `AccessGroupBudgetRequest` also has `budget_id`. From reading the code, the same `TypeError` should hit it once the group has a budget row. Not reproduced.

title: [Bug]: spend_logs_metadata is never recorded for /v1beta/interactions

judge.reasoning: Both patches apply the same one-line fix the issue verified (adding "interactions" to LITELLM_METADATA_ROUTES), and all five independent tests pass on both, so they are equal on the reported scenarios. Patch A additionally hardens the merge helper the issue names as root-cause step 3: add_missing_spend_metadata_to_litellm_metadata now carries spend_logs_metadata across when `metadata` is demonstrably the proxy's request bucket (it holds user_api_key stamps) and litellm_metadata does not already define the key. That guard preserves the /responses convention that provider body `metadata` is not recorded (covered by an explicit test), keeps a caller-supplied litellm_metadata value authoritative, and extends the fix to other generic-API routes (videos, vector_stores, containers) where the same split happens, which the issue itself flags as the broader alternative and as the cause of related breakage. The change is small, conditional, and documented, so the added risk is low relative to the coverage it gains. On tests, A is stronger: it exercises the real get_logging_payload path to the spend-log row for both header and body litellm_metadata on both interaction paths, plus unit tests for the helper's new carry and non-carry cases. Patch B's tests are sound but narrower (route classification plus a hand-simulated router update feeding get_litellm_metadata_from_kwargs). Both patches' new tests depend on helpers/imports not visible in the diffs, so that uncertainty is shared. B is a clean minimal fix; A is the same fix plus a targeted, well-guarded root-cause repair with better test coverage, so A is the better patch.

issue_md:
### Description

On the proxy, `spend_logs_metadata` sent with a Gemini Interactions API request (`POST /v1beta/interactions`, `call_type=acreate_interaction`) never reaches `LiteLLM_SpendLogs`: `metadata.spend_logs_metadata` is `null` on every row, whichever way it is sent (`x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata` header, body `metadata.spend_logs_metadata` or body `litellm_metadata.spend_logs_metadata`). The same three ways work on `/v1/chat/completions` against the same deployment. Tags and the session id do arrive. Anyone who attributes spend through `spend_logs_metadata` loses it on the Interactions route.

Expected: the header and `litellm_metadata` (as on `/v1/responses`) land in `metadata.spend_logs_metadata`.

Seen on v1.106.1 and v1.104.0.

**Root cause** (traced on v1.106.1 with a debug hook that logged key names at each step):

1. `interactions` is not in `LITELLM_METADATA_ROUTES` (`litellm/proxy/litellm_pre_call_utils.py`), so the proxy puts the request metadata (`spend_logs_metadata`, `tags`, `user_api_key_*`) under `metadata`.
2. The router puts the deployment metadata (`model_group`, `deployment`, `model_info`, `api_base`, retry fields) under `litellm_metadata`, so `litellm.interactions.create` receives both dicts.
3. `get_logging_payload` (`litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/spend_tracking_utils.py`) reads them through `get_litellm_metadata_from_kwargs` (`litellm/litellm_core_utils/core_helpers.py`). That function returns `litellm_metadata` whenever it is non-empty, after `add_missing_spend_metadata_to_litellm_metadata` has copied over only the keys containing `user_api_key`. So `spend_logs_metadata` is dropped there, even though `kwargs["litellm_params"]["metadata"]["spend_logs_metadata"]` and `standard_logging_object["metadata"]["spend_logs_metadata"]` both still hold it at that point.

**Candidate fix, verified locally:** route `/interactions` like `/responses`.

```diff
 LITELLM_METADATA_ROUTES: Final = (
     "batches",
     "bedrock",
     "/v1/messages",
     "responses",
     "files",
+    "interactions",
 )
```

With that line, the header and body `litellm_metadata` are both recorded on `/v1beta/interactions`; body `metadata` is not, which matches the `/v1/responses` convention. Chat completions are unchanged. A broader alternative would be to have `add_missing_spend_metadata_to_litellm_metadata` also carry over `spend_logs_metadata` (as #47790 did for `litellm_received_at`), which would cover any other route where the two dicts split.

Related: #34905 (the same merge helper drops the router's `model_group` when a guardrail plants `litellm_metadata`), #47790 (merged 2026-10-21; carries `litellm_received_at` across the same merge, not `spend_logs_metadata`), #39749 (`store: false` rows dropped on this route, which is why the repro below uses `store: true`).

### Config

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gemini-3.1-flash-lite
    litellm_params:
      model: gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-lite
      api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
```

### LiteLLM Version

v1.106.1

### Steps to Repro

Proxy: official `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.1` image with Postgres and the config above.

1. Request:
   ```bash
   curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1beta/interactions \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -H "x-litellm-session-id: probe-session" \
     -H 'x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata: {"probe": "header"}' \
     -d '{"model": "gemini-3.1-flash-lite", "input": "Reply with the single word OK.", "store": true}'
   ```

title: [Bug]: /v1/messages/count_tokens returns 500 for a `search_result` block, and for any content block type the local counter does not list

judge.reasoning: Both patches fix the issue the same way at the root: a `search_result` TypedDict, a counting branch for title/source/content, a `ValueError` subclass for unknown block types, and a mapping of that subclass to a 400 `invalid_request_error`. All ten independent tests pass on both, so correctness is equal on the issue's scenarios. The differences are in where the 400 is produced and what the client sees. Patch B maps the error inside `count_request_tokens` in proxy_server.py, around the local estimate call, so every caller of the shared counting path (not only the Anthropic route) stops answering 500, and it emits a clean message ("Token counting does not support content blocks of type 'future_block'") carrying the type on the exception and preserving the chain with `from e`. Patch A maps it only in the Anthropic endpoint and returns the internal wrapped string as the client message ("Error getting number of tokens from content list: Invalid content item type: ... default_token_count=None"), which names the type but leaks counter internals; its `raise (X if isinstance(...) else ValueError)(...)` re-raise is also awkward. B's TypedDict includes the documented `cache_control`/`citations` fields consistent with the neighbouring document param and has an explicit `_count_search_result_tokens` that recurses through `_count_content_list` for nested content; A reuses the generic `_count_anthropic_content` and adds the type to the user/tool_result unions, which is reasonable too. On tests, A is slightly stronger: it includes a negative control (an `image` without `source` still yields 500 api_error) and a default_token_count fallback check, while B covers unit, nested, and endpoint-level 200/400 cases without that control. Weighing craft of the fix and user-facing error quality over A's marginally better tests, B is the better patch.

issue_md:
### Description

`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` answers HTTP 500 when a message contains a `search_result` content block, which is a documented Messages content block ([Search results](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/search-results)). The same happens for any block type the local token counter does not know, so a client that counts a conversation before sending it (as coding agents do for context management) gets a server error instead of a count or a clean refusal.

Expected: `count_tokens` accepts the same content as `/v1/messages` and returns `{"input_tokens": n}` (for `search_result`, counting its `title`, `source` and `content` text, as the other text-bearing blocks are counted); a block type it cannot count is refused with a 400 `invalid_request_error` naming the type, per the Anthropic [Token counting](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/token-counting) guide ("supports the same structured list of inputs" as Messages). Never a 500.

Observed on LiteLLM 1.105.1 / vLLM 0.31.0 dev build, 2026-10-22. (On 1.105.1 the body is FastAPI's `{"detail": ...}`; #46815 moves it to the Anthropic envelope in 1.105.3 / 1.106.2, but the status stays whatever the route maps a `ValueError` to.)

### Config

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: glm-5.3
    litellm_params:
      model: hosted_vllm/zai-org/GLM-5.3
      api_base: http://<vllm-host>:8000/v1
```

### LiteLLM Version

v1.105.1

### Steps to Repro

1. A `search_result` block:

```sh
curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' http://localhost:4000/v1/messages/count_tokens \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_API_KEY" -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"glm-5.3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"search_result","source":"https://docs.example.invalid/notes","title":"Project notes","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The code word is 7f3a."}]},{"type":"text","text":"Reply with only the code word you were given, or NONE."}]}]}'
```

HTTP 500:

```json
{"detail":{"error":"Internal server error: Error getting number of tokens from content list: Invalid content item type: search_result. Expected str or dict with 'type' field (text, image_url, image, document, file, tool_use, tool_result, thinking, redacted_thinking, tool_reference)., default_token_count=None"}}
```

2. A block type the counter does not list (a stand-in for a block introduced by a newer client):

```sh
curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' http://localhost:4000/v1/messages/count_tokens \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_API_KEY" -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"glm-5.3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Reply with the single word: ok"},{"type":"future_block","future_block":{"value":"ignore me"}}]}]}'
```

HTTP 500, same message with `Invalid content item type: future_block`.

3. Expected: (1) HTTP 200 `{"input_tokens": <n>}`; (2) HTTP 400 `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"... future_block ..."}}`. Control on the same proxy: the same request with a `document`, `image`, `tool_result` or `redacted_thinking` block instead returns 200 with a count.

Possible cause (a lead, not a confirmed cause): `_count_content_list()` in `litellm/litellm_core_utils/token_counter.py` handles `text`, `image_url`, `image`, `document`, `file`, `tool_use`, `tool_result`, `thinking`, `redacted_thinking` and `tool_reference`, and raises `ValueError("Invalid content item type: ...")` for anything else; the route turns that into a 500. On main the list is the same. A `search_result` branch (count `title`, `source` and the text in `content`), and mapping the remaining `ValueError` to a 400 rather than a 500, would cover both cases. We have not run main, where #46772 added a 400 for blocks the OpenAI and Gemini count conversions cannot handle; it is not clear to us whether that path is taken for a locally counted `hosted_vllm` deployment.

Related: #44784 (open, same error for `compaction` blocks), #47858 (open, `tool_addition` / `tool_removal`), #46772 (merged), #46815 (merged, error envelope).

### Which part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy core: startup, config, health checks, endpoints

### How are you deploying?

Other

title: [Bug]: Bedrock claude_platform/ requests are logged with $0 spend

judge.reasoning: Both patches fix the exact scenarios in the issue (bedrock/claude_platform/claude-opus-5-5 and the bare claude_platform/ form), and the independent tests confirm that. The difference is in how. Patch A addresses the root cause the issue names: it adds claude_platform/ to strip_bedrock_routing_prefix and overrides BedrockModelInfo.get_model_cost_key to map a Claude API id onto the existing Bedrock key (anthropic.<id>, with -v1:0 / -v1 fallbacks, verified against the cost map before use). This generalizes to any Claude model already priced for Bedrock, and for ids it cannot map it now raises ModelNotMappedError instead of the silent $0 fallback the issue complained about (seen in the claude-sonnet-4-5 alias run). Its tests directly reproduce the issue's cost_per_token/get_model_info/completion_cost calls and would fail on base. Patch B instead adds ~600 lines of per-model JSON entries (duplicated in two files) under bedrock/claude_platform/<id>, which works only for models explicitly listed and leaves the silent-zero path intact for anything else (the dated claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 id still returns (0.0, 0.0) under B, exactly the failure mode reported). B also changes bedrock cost_per_token for every Bedrock model to apply a geo multiplier, a behavior change beyond the issue's ask that adds risk, and it has to whitelist claude_platform entries in an unrelated test. B's test is reasonable but data-driven over its own entries rather than over the issue's scenarios. A is the smaller, root-cause fix with stronger targeted tests; B masks the symptom with data and carries extra scope.

issue_md:
### Description

Every request routed through Claude Platform on AWS (`bedrock/claude_platform/<model>`, or `claude_platform/<model>` with
provider `bedrock`) gets `spend = 0` in `LiteLLM_SpendLogs`. The proxy returns no `x-litellm-response-cost` header and
logs no cost-calculation error, so budgets and spend reports silently under-count Claude usage.

Other Bedrock routes for the same models are priced correctly. Examples: `bedrock/converse/anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`,
`bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`.

## Cause

Claude Platform on AWS takes Claude API model IDs (`claude-opus-5-5`). The cost map stores Bedrock pricing under
Bedrock model IDs (`anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`), and no entry exists for `claude_platform/...`.

- `strip_bedrock_routing_prefix` does not remove `claude_platform/`, so `get_model_info` searches for
  `claude_platform/claude-opus-5-5`.
- `BedrockModelInfo` does not override `get_model_cost_key`, so nothing maps the Claude API ID to the Bedrock key.
- The lookup then falls back to a capability-only entry with zero costs instead of raising, so the miss is silent.

Adding `claude_platform/` to `strip_bedrock_routing_prefix` alone is not enough. The lookup then searches for
`claude-opus-5-5` under provider `bedrock`. That key belongs to provider `anthropic`, so it is rejected and the cost is still 0.

## Relevant log output

```
spend=0.0 model=claude_platform/claude-opus-5-5 custom_llm_provider=bedrock prompt_tokens=11 completion_tokens=5
model_map_information.model_map_key=claude_platform/claude-opus-5-5
```

```yaml
  - model_name: claude-opus-5-5
    litellm_params:

      aws_region_name: eu-west-1
      workspace_id: wrkspc_...
```

1.106.2

```yaml
  - model_name: claude-opus-5-5

      model: bedrock/claude_platform/claude-opus-5-5
```

```python
# (0.0, 0.0)  — expected (4.0, 20.0), same as anthropic.claude-opus-5-5

litellm.cost_per_token(model="anthropic.claude-opus-5-5", custom_llm_provider="bedrock",
                       prompt_tokens=1_000_000, completion_tokens=1_000_000)
# (4.0, 20.0)
```

With `model: claude_platform/claude-opus-5-5` (no `bedrock/` prefix) and provider `bedrock`, spend is also 0. The spend
log shows `model_map_key: claude_platform/claude-opus-5-5`.


### Which part of LiteLLM is this about?

Spend tracking: spend logs, cost attribution, usage reports

Docker

title: [Bug]: Bulk Invite Users – "Download CSV Template" button has no onClick handler (still unfixed, #27197 closed as stale).

judge.reasoning: Both patches wire the same onClick fix with an identical header row (user_email,user_role,teams,max_budget,budget_duration,models), so correctness of the core issue is equal. The differences are in the example data and tests. Patch A's example row populates teams with placeholder IDs (team-id-1,team-id-2) that the upload's team validation would reject, so a user who downloads the template and uploads it unmodified would see validation errors; Patch B deliberately leaves teams blank and documents why, and its example rows use only valid roles and a numeric budget, matching the issue's note on valid roles. Patch B's tests are stronger: besides checking the blob, filename and header, they round-trip the generated CSV back through the component's upload step and assert both rows appear with no 'Invalid' marker, which is the behaviour the issue actually asks for; a separate unit test validates the template builder's structure and role validity. Patch A's test is reasonable but lacks try/finally cleanup and uses toHaveBeenCalledOnce on a prototype spy that B's comment indicates is already a shared mock in setupTests, making A's count assertion potentially leak state from earlier tests. Patch A earns some craft credit for reusing the existing downloadBlob utility rather than duplicating anchor-download logic, and B's extra module is a slight scope increase, but neither offsets B's more correct example data and more meaningful test coverage. Independent tests were skipped on all trees and provide no signal.

title: auth failure handler 500s on any non-object JSON body (AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get')

judge.reasoning: Both patches stop the AttributeError at its source (the handler now works on a dict-or-empty view of the body) and both make the surrogate-repair fallback in read_request_body stop handing a raw list/scalar to callers, which is the path that still 500s on current main (the independent tests show only the NaN/Infinity/1e400 cases fail on base, i.e. the json.loads repair branch). All independent tests pass on both. The difference is scope and risk. Patch A is a tight fix: an isinstance guard in the handler, a small _json_object_body helper applied to both parse paths so a non-object body consistently yields {}, and tests at three layers (handler with every body shape from the issue including BudgetExceededError, end-to-end user_api_key_auth with raw bytes including the repair-fallback inputs, and read_request_body itself). Patch B goes much further: it turns pydantic ValidationError into a 400 inside read_request_body and then bolts on a route-sniffing carve-out (importing pass-through and lens modules into http_parsing_utils, inspecting request.scope['route'], checking APIRoute.body_field.is_required() and whether the stripped body equals b'null'). That heuristic is fragile and coupled: it had to add path_params to an unrelated vertex pass-through test to keep it working, it rewrites the protobuf and lens buffering tests, and any non-pass-through endpoint that legitimately accepts a list body would now get a 400 from the auth dependency with no carve-out. It also changes _parse_binary_body behaviour. None of that is required by the issue, which explicitly accepts 'the normal 401', and it adds surface for regressions that A does not. B's handler-side change (as_str_mapping, widening the parameter type to object) is fine, and its parametrized classification test is good, but the parsing-layer redesign counts against it. A resolves the issue at the root with less risk and adequate, non-tautological tests.

issue_md:
### Bug Report

**Describe the bug**

Any request whose JSON body is valid JSON but not an object (`[]`, `null`, `"s"`, `1`, `true`) causes an
unhandled `AttributeError` and a **500** on unauthenticated endpoints. The auth failure handler assumes the
parsed body is a dict and calls `.get()` on it.

**To Reproduce**

No API key needed:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '[]'
```

Result: `500 Internal Server Error`. `{}` correctly gives 401, so the difference is purely the body type.

All of these 500: `[]`, `[1]`, `[1,2]`, `null`, `"s"`, `1`, `true`, `[[]]`, `[[1]]`.

**Traceback**

```
File "litellm/proxy/auth/user_api_key_auth.py", line 2280, in user_api_key_auth_builder
    return await UserAPIKeyAuthExceptionHandler.handle_authentication_error(
File "litellm/proxy/auth/auth_exception_handler.py", line 222, in handle_authentication_error
    model=request_data.get("model"),
AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'
```

**Root cause**

`litellm/proxy/auth/auth_exception_handler.py`:

```python
seed_request_identity(
    user_api_key_dict,
    model=request_data.get("model"),
)
```

and again a few lines later:

```python
budget_model: Final = request_data.get("model")
```

`request_data` is whatever `json.loads` produced, so it is only a dict when the client sent an object. There is
no `isinstance(request_data, dict)` guard.

**Expected behavior**

A non-object body on an unauthenticated request should give the normal 401 (or a 4xx validation error), not a
500 with a traceback.

**Your Environment**

- LiteLLM 1.106.3 (`litellm/litellm:latest`); the same unguarded lines are present on current `main`
- Linux, aarch64, official container image
- Default config, no database

**Impact**

Unauthenticated 500 + traceback per request, trivially triggerable by any client. Low severity (DoS-ish /
log noise), but it is on the auth-failure path, so it fires for every malformed client that sends an array.

title: [Bug]: Admin UI Router Settings renders no input for String-typed general_settings fields (spend-log retention, cleanup run budget/timeout)

judge.reasoning: The independent tests give no signal: every run on base, A and B failed with the same FileNotFoundError for the node binary, so the verdict rests on the diffs. Both patches fix the root cause the same way, by adding a `String` branch to SettingValueEditor that renders an Input with aria-label, shows the stored value, and feeds onChange so Update submits the typed value; both add integration tests that would fail before and pass after. The difference is at the edges. Patch A mirrors the existing List handling: it trims input, maps an emptied field to null, and extends the update handler so an emptied String field triggers handleResetField (delete) rather than an update, and its key on stored_in_db makes the uncontrolled input reset after a delete, matching the List branch's visible convention. Patch B passes the raw string through, so clearing the box and clicking Update sends an empty string to updateConfigFieldSetting and stores "" in the DB for duration-style settings like retention periods, which is an untested and likely harmful state the existing code deliberately avoids for Select/List. B's controlled input is fine but offers no equivalent safeguard. B's test does usefully exercise the trash-icon reset path, and A's tests cover display, update with trimming, and clear-on-empty; test quality is comparable. On correctness at the issue's edges and consistency with surrounding conventions, A is the better fix.

On the Admin UI page `/ui/router-settings/` (General Settings card), every general_settings field whose `field_type` is `"String"` renders an **empty value cell — no input control at all**. title: [Bug]: Gemini grounding annotations drop additional sources for a passage

judge.reasoning:
Both patches fix the root cause the same way: they replace the `chunk_indices[0]` lookup with a loop over every index in `groundingChunkIndices`, skipping indices absent from `chunk_to_uri_map`. The independent tests confirm both pass all three scenarios (two web sources, non-web first source, several multi-source passages) where base fails. Correctness is equal; Patch B dropping the `chunk_indices` truthiness check is harmless since iterating an empty list emits nothing.

The difference is in tests and craft. Patch B adds two explicit, separately named tests that map one-to-one onto the two scenarios called out in the issue (multiple web sources per passage, and web sources following a non-web first index), with literal expected annotations that are easy to read and that reproduce the issue's own example exactly. They are placed next to the existing `test_vertex_ai_annotation_conversion` tests, matching the surrounding file's conventions. Patch A's single parametrized test does cover both scenarios (via `[2, 1, 0]` with a retrievedContext chunk) plus an extra support, but its expected value is built by a list comprehension over the input, which is harder to read and edges toward re-deriving the result rather than stating it. Patch B's early `continue` on a missing segment also flattens nesting and its comment states why multiple annotations are emitted.

These are small margins, but B's tests communicate the fix more directly and sit with related tests, so B is the better patch.

issue_md:
### Description

Gemini can attach several sources to the same grounded passage, but LiteLLM converts only the first source index to an annotation. The other source associations are lost even when Google returned them

### Config

This reproduces directly in the Google grounding converter, without credentials or a proxy configuration

### LiteLLM Version

1.109.0, current main at f1795e6d447a4e5a3660de0d2fde5e1f44f52929

### Steps to Repro

Run the following against an unmodified checkout

```python
from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.gemini.vertex_and_google_ai_studio_gemini import VertexGeminiConfig

metadata = {
    "groundingChunks": [
        {"web": {"uri": "https://example.com/a", "title": "A"}},
        {"web": {"uri": "https://example.com/b", "title": "B"}},
    ],
    "groundingSupports": [
        {
            "segment": {"startIndex": 0, "endIndex": 5},
            "groundingChunkIndices": [0, 1],
        }
    ],
}
annotations = VertexGeminiConfig._convert_grounding_metadata_to_annotations([metadata], "Claim")
print(annotations)
```

Actual output

```python
[{'type': 'url_citation', 'url_citation': {'start_index': 0, 'end_index': 5, 'url': 'https://example.com/a', 'title': 'A'}}]
```

Expected output

```python
[
    {'type': 'url_citation', 'url_citation': {'start_index': 0, 'end_index': 5, 'url': 'https://example.com/a', 'title': 'A'}},
    {'type': 'url_citation', 'url_citation': {'start_index': 0, 'end_index': 5, 'url': 'https://example.com/b', 'title': 'B'}},
]
```

The converter reads `chunk_indices[0]` instead of iterating over all source indices. If the first index points to a non-web chunk, later valid web sources are lost too

This reproduces locally using synthetic grounding metadata. Fresh direct Gemini API calls through a local LiteLLM proxy also reproduced it on 2026-10-28. The unmodified base retained 12 of 18 source associations. The fixed converter retained all 19 of 19 source associations in a separate generation, with matching URLs, titles and text ranges. Each call contained six passages with multiple web sources, and counts were compared within each response

### Which part of LiteLLM is this about?

LLM translation: a specific provider's request or response

### How are you deploying?

pip / Python SDK

Related streaming issue #48744 covers citation events after Chat Completions conversion

title: key model allowlist is enforced per-route, so generateContent, streamGenerateContent and image routes still serve a denied model (gap left by #41852)

judge.reasoning:
Both patches close the three routes named in the issue, and the independent tests confirm it: all four denied-URL cases go from FAIL-ASSERT on base to PASS on both A and B, with the controls unchanged. The difference is in how each gets there and what else it risks.

Patch A changes `get_model_from_request` to prefer the URL model whenever the FastAPI-dispatched handler actually binds a `model`/`model_name` path parameter or a `model` query parameter, read from `scope["route"]`. That is route-agnostic in the sense the issue asks for: generateContent, streamGenerateContent, the deployment image routes, `/engines/{model}/...`, `/openai/deployments/{model}/chat/...` and `?model=` are all covered without a template list, and any future `{model}` handler is covered automatically. It also only trusts path params the handler declares, so the budget-fallback's planted `path_params["model"]` does not leak into routes that never read it (tested explicitly). It keeps the rest of the existing resolution flow intact by assigning into `model` and letting the remaining post-processing run. The change is confined to auth_utils, and its tests are end-to-end through the real app with TestClient, asserting both the 403 and that the premium deployment's mock output never appears, plus positive cases (allowed URL model with denied body model is served, streaming, multipart edits). Those are exactly the issue's reproduction scenarios.

Patch B hardcodes three regexes for the affected routes and replays `resolve_inference_model` with general_settings/user_model to mirror the handler's precedence, then threads `path_params` through the budget-reservation estimators. It is correct for the listed routes and the reservation work is a reasonable adjacent improvement, but it is the template-list approach the issue explicitly warns leaves other routes (e.g. `/engines/{model}/`, `?model=`) and future routes open. It also returns early before the remainder of `get_model_from_request`'s candidate/post-processing logic, skipping whatever normalization follows, and it spreads the change across five production files (including a new `user_model_view` in proxy_server and an intra-function import of proxy_server), which widens the blast radius for a fix the issue scopes to the access check. Its tests are solid unit tests but mostly exercise `get_model_from_request` directly rather than the served path.

On correctness both resolve the reported bypass; A addresses the root cause more generally and with less churn, and its tests more directly reproduce the issue. B's extra reservation plumbing is neutral-to-slightly-risky scope. A wins on a moderate margin.

issue_md:
## what happens a virtual key is scoped to one model with `models: ["cheap-model"]`. the proxy correctly blocks the denied model when it is named in the request **body** (403 `key_model_access_denied`). but on three routes the key is served the denied model anyway, as long as the denied model is in the **url** and an allowed model is in the body: - `POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent` - `POST /v1beta/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent` - `POST /openai/deployments/{model}/images/generations` (and `/images/edits`) the model that actually runs is not bounded by the key's allowed list on these routes. this is the same class as the open report #41810 (chat route) and its open fix #41852. that fix only lists the chat / completions / embeddings routes, so these routes stay open after it. i applied #41852 and re-tested: the chat routes become 403, but generateContent, streamGenerateContent and images still return 200 and serve the denied model. ## why it happens two parts of the proxy read the requested model from different places. ```mermaid flowchart TB R["one request"] --> B["body says: cheap-model (allowed)"] R --> U["url path says: premium-model (denied)"] B --> G{"access check reads the BODY
get_model_from_request -> allow"} U --> H{"handler routes on the URL
resolve_inference_model prefers endpoint model"} G --> P["request passes the check"] H --> S["denied model is served and billed"] P --> S ``` - the access check `get_model_from_request` (`litellm/proxy/auth/auth_utils.py`) reads the body `model` first, and only falls back to the url model when the body has none. with an allowed model in the body, it approves. - the handler passes the url path model into the request processor (`litellm/proxy/google_endpoints/endpoints.py`, `litellm/proxy/image_endpoints/endpoints.py`), and `resolve_inference_model` (`litellm/proxy/common_utils/http_parsing_utils.py`) prefers that endpoint model over the body. so routing uses the denied model. the safety net only works when the body is silent: with no body model the access check reads the url model and correctly returns 403. the bypass needs both fields, an allowed body model to pass the check and a denied url model for the handler to route on. ## exact reproduction tested on `main` `1176e608b19` (2026-10-28), also on `cfe0100e` / `v1.106.4`. no provider keys needed; the two upstreams below are local stubs, so the served model is visible in the forwarded request. config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: cheap-model litellm_params: model: openai/cheap-upstream api_base: http://127.0.0.1:4190/v1 api_key: dummy - model_name: premium-model litellm_params: model: openai/premium-upstream api_base: http://127.0.0.1:4190/v1 api_key: dummy general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY ``` make a key scoped to the cheap model only: ```bash curl -s $PROXY/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" \ -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"models":["cheap-model"]}' ``` control, denied model in the body, correctly blocked: ```bash curl -s $PROXY/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"premium-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' # HTTP 403 # {"error":{"message":"The requested model 'premium-model' is not available for this API key ...","type":"key_model_access_denied","code":"403"}} ``` bypass, denied model in the url, allowed model in the body: ```bash curl -s "$PROXY/v1beta/models/premium-model:generateContent" -H "x-goog-api-key: $KEY" \ -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"cheap-model","contents":[{"role":"user","parts":[{"text":"hi"}]}]}' # HTTP 200 ``` the forwarded request to the upstream shows the denied model actually ran: ``` POST /v1/chat/completions {"model":"premium-upstream","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]} ``` the same works on `:streamGenerateContent` and on `POST /openai/deployments/premium-model/images/generations` with body `{"model":"cheap-model","prompt":"..."}`. ## results each case run 5 times, on stock `main` and on `main` with the open fix #41852 applied. "served" is the model id in the forwarded upstream request. | route, with denied model in url and allowed in body | stock main | main + #41852 | |---|---|---| | `/v1/chat/completions?model=` | 200, served denied | **403** (fixed) | | `/openai/deployments/{denied}/chat/completions` | 200, served denied | **403** (fixed) | | `:generateContent` | 200, served denied | **200, still served denied** | | `:streamGenerateContent` | 200, served denied | **200, still served denied** | | `/openai/deployments/{denied}/images/generations` | 200, served denied | **200, still served denied** | | control: denied model in body | 403 | 403 | | control: allowed in url and body | 200, served allowed | 200, served allowed | | control: `/v1/messages?model=denied` body allowed | 200, served allowed (not affected) | 200, served allowed | billing follows the served model: on generateContent the denied model is billed to the key at its rate. a fresh key scoped to the cheap model with `max_budget: 1.0` is drained by five generateContent calls and the sixth returns `422 budget_exceeded`, so the denied model also spends against the key's budget. a full writeup with the raw request/response/forwarded bytes, the 5-of-5 matrix, the fix-control run, and the spend rows is here, with plain-language diagrams: https://kairo-allowlist-explainer.vercel.app ## why this matters the per-key `models` list is the operator's way to bound cost and model access for a key (for example a key limited to one cheap or local model for a tenant). on these routes that boundary is not enforced, so a key holder reaches and spends on models the operator never granted. it is a `403` on the body today, so the gap is a per-route inconsistency, not a design choice. honest scope: this needs a valid authenticated key and a hand-written request (the google genai sdks send the model only in the url, no body model, which is correctly blocked). so it is a scoped key holder bypassing their own scope, not an unauthenticated attack or a cross-tenant data leak. by the categories in `SECURITY.md` this is a p2 (authenticated action beyond permissions). i am raising it here because the same class is already public in #41810 and #41852; happy to move it to a private advisory with a screen recording if you prefer that channel. ## suggested fix (route-agnostic, so new routes are covered too) #41852 fixes this by listing route templates. that works for the routes it lists, but any route not on the list (these three, and any added later) stays open. ```mermaid flowchart LR Fix["#41852 route list"] -->|covers| Chat["chat / completions / embeddings"] Fix -.->|misses| Gc["generateContent / streamGenerateContent"] Fix -.->|misses| Img["images routes"] Fix -.->|misses| New["any future route"] ``` every model-serving route funnels through one place, `ProxyBaseLLMRequestProcessing.base_process_llm_request` in `litellm/proxy/common_request_processing.py`, right after `resolve_inference_model` sets `self.data["model"]` to the model that will actually run. re-checking the key and team allowlist against that resolved model there (reusing `can_key_call_model` / `can_team_access_model` from `auth_checks.py`, and honoring the existing router-fallback access rules) closes every route at once, because it checks the model that is truly dispatched rather than guessing per route. ```mermaid flowchart TB A["chat"] --> F B["generateContent / stream"] --> F C["images"] --> F D["responses, messages, video, ocr, ... (one funnel)"] --> F F["base_process_llm_request
self.data['model'] = resolve_inference_model(...)"] --> K{"re-check the resolved model
against the key/team allowlist"} K -->|allowed| Run["dispatch"] K -->|not allowed| Deny["403 key_model_access_denied"] ``` i have this fix working locally and can open a pr with tests that cover generateContent, images and a chat route if that direction is welcome. i am also glad to add the image and generateContent templates to #41852 instead if you would rather keep the current approach.

judge.reasoning: The issue names the root cause explicitly: a shared Logging object carries has_logged_async_success/has_logged_sync_success across router retries, so the later successful attempt's success log is skipped. Patch A only handles the proxy's deferred ("parked") success result: in carry_failed_attempt_usage it moves a parked deferred_success_result into failed_attempts_usage so the serving attempt bills it. That fixes the proxy reproduction (both proxy tests pass) but leaves the non-deferred case untouched: when the first attempt's success log has already been emitted or enqueued (has_logged_async_success set), the retry's success log is still suppressed. The independent test that exercises exactly that quoted root cause (Router.acompletion with a shared logging object, first attempt already logged) still fails on A with recorded_costs=[0.147], identical to base. Patch B addresses both paths: it detects a superseded attempt that already logged or enqueued its success (async enqueued, sync scheduled, or has_logged_* set), clears the one-success-per-request markers and stale cost/usage state so the retry logs and prices its own response, and uses pending counters so the in-flight first-attempt log's completion marker does not re-suppress the retry; it separately handles the parked deferred result by carrying it as a served round. It also marks sync success logs as scheduled in utils.client so the sync executor path is covered. All three independent tests pass on B. B's tests are more substantive too: proxy-level chat, messages-refusal and retry scenarios plus router-level shared-logging tests, including a sync in-flight log race, versus A's single unit test that only drives the parked path through manual calls. B is larger and more intricate, which carries some risk, but the added state is targeted and documented, whereas A leaves the issue's stated root cause unfixed. B wins on correctness and tests.

issue_md:
### What happened?

When a retryable error is raised after a non-streaming provider response has already completed success processing, the router retries with the same `Logging` object. The first attempt has already set `has_logged_async_success`/`has_logged_sync_success`, so success logging for the later successful attempt is skipped.

This causes the final response usage and reported cost to describe different attempts. In the reproduction, the response body contains the final attempt's cache-read usage, while both the accounting callback and `x-litellm-response-cost` retain only the discarded first attempt's cache-write cost.

For example, a provider can return a billable response marked as a content-policy refusal. LiteLLM maps that provider refusal to `ContentPolicyViolationError` and retries. If the retry succeeds, its cost is then skipped because the first attempt already marked success logging as complete.

### Reproduction

The test below uses only stock LiteLLM APIs and a local fake Bedrock endpoint. The first response is fully priced, then the test raises `ContentPolicyViolationError`; the configured router retry succeeds with different usage.

Save as `test_retry_cost_accounting_upstream_repro.py`, then run:

```bash
pip install 'litellm[proxy]==1.104.5' pytest pytest-asyncio
pytest -q test_retry_cost_accounting_upstream_repro.py
```

Observed on `litellm[proxy]==1.104.5`:

```text
AssertionError: recorded_costs=[0.147], header_cost=0.147
Expected records: [0.147, 0.036]
Expected measurable request cost: 0.183
```

The request itself succeeds with HTTP 200, reports one attempted retry, and its response body contains the final attempt's cache-read usage.

### Root cause

`Router.async_function_with_retries` carries `litellm_logging_obj` into later attempts. In `litellm/litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py`, `Logging.should_run_logging()` returns false once the shared object contains `has_logged_<success event> = True`. As a result, the later attempt does not run `_process_hidden_params_and_response_cost` and does not emit its accounting event.

The proxy subsequently reads stale first-attempt state when constructing `x-litellm-response-cost`.

### Expected behavior

Every provider response with billable usage should be accounted exactly once, including a later successful attempt after a post-response retry. The request-level cost must not silently omit later attempts. Please confirm whether `x-litellm-response-cost` is intended to aggregate all billable attempts; the missing final-attempt accounting record is a defect independently of that public header contract.

### Affected area

- Router retries after post-response errors
- Non-streaming success logging/accounting
- Reproduced with Anthropic Messages semantics through Bedrock

Related but distinct from #26475, #37105, #40736, #19216, and #42663.

+"""
+A provider response the router discards for a retry or a fallback (a content-filtered chat choice, a
+safeguard refusal, an error raised after the response was served) was billed by the provider. The
+proxy parks the request's success log until its post-call hooks run, so the discarded attempt must
+not take the success log from the response the client receives, nor drop out of its cost.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator, Mapping
+from typing import Final
+
+import httpx
+import pytest
+import respx
+from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
+
+import litellm
+from litellm import Router
+from litellm.integrations.custom_logger import CustomLogger
+from litellm.proxy import proxy_server
+from litellm.proxy._types import UserAPIKeyAuth
+from litellm.proxy.auth.user_api_key_auth import user_api_key_auth
+
+INPUT_RATE: Final = 0.001
+OUTPUT_RATE: Final = 0.002
+PROMPT_TOKENS: Final = 10
+FIRST_COMPLETION_TOKENS: Final = 10
+FINAL_COMPLETION_TOKENS: Final = 20
+FIRST_COST: Final = PROMPT_TOKENS * INPUT_RATE + FIRST_COMPLETION_TOKENS * OUTPUT_RATE
+FINAL_COST: Final = PROMPT_TOKENS * INPUT_RATE + FINAL_COMPLETION_TOKENS * OUTPUT_RATE
+PRICING: Final = {"input_cost_per_token": INPUT_RATE, "output_cost_per_token": OUTPUT_RATE}
+
+
+class _SuccessCosts(CustomLogger):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.costs: tuple[object, ...] = ()
+
+    async def async_log_success_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time) -> None:  # noqa: ANN001  # CustomLogger's untyped hook signature
+        self.costs = (*self.costs, kwargs.get("response_cost"))
+
+
+def _chat_body(attempt: int, finish_reason: str) -> dict[str, object]:  # mutable-ok: a JSON body
+    completion_tokens: Final = FIRST_COMPLETION_TOKENS if attempt == 1 else FINAL_COMPLETION_TOKENS
+    return {
+        "id": f"chatcmpl-attempt-{attempt}",
+        "object": "chat.completion",
+        "created": 1,
+        "model": "gpt-4o",
+        "choices": [
+            {
+                "index": 0,
+                "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": f"attempt {attempt}"},
+                "finish_reason": finish_reason,
+            }
+        ],
+        "usage": {
+            "prompt_tokens": PROMPT_TOKENS,
+            "completion_tokens": completion_tokens,
+            "total_tokens": PROMPT_TOKENS + completion_tokens,
+        },
+    }
+
+
+def _messages_body(attempt: int) -> dict[str, object]:  # mutable-ok: a JSON body
+    refused: Final = attempt == 1
+    return {
+        "id": f"msg_attempt_{attempt}",
+        "type": "message",
+        "role": "assistant",
+        "model": "claude-test",
+        "content": [{"type": "text", "text": f"attempt {attempt}"}],
+        "stop_reason": "refusal" if refused else "end_turn",
+        **({"stop_details": {"type": "refusal", "category": None, "explanation": "declined"}} if refused else {}),
+        "stop_sequence": None,
+        "usage": {
+            "input_tokens": PROMPT_TOKENS,
+            "output_tokens": FIRST_COMPLETION_TOKENS if refused else FINAL_COMPLETION_TOKENS,
+        },
+    }
+
+
+def _deployment(name: str, model: str) -> dict[str, object]:  # mutable-ok: a model_list entry
+    return {"model_name": name, "litellm_params": {"model": model, "api_key": "test-key"}, "model_info": PRICING}
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def success_costs(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> _SuccessCosts:
+    capture: Final = _SuccessCosts()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(litellm, "disable_aiohttp_transport", True)
+    monkeypatch.setenv("LITELLM_DANGEROUSLY_PERMIT_WEAK_OR_UNSET_MASTER_KEY", "true")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(litellm, "callbacks", [])
+    monkeypatch.setattr(litellm, "success_callback", [])
+    monkeypatch.setattr(litellm, "_async_success_callback", [capture])
+    return capture
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def proxy_post(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+) -> Iterator[Callable[[Router, str, Mapping[str, object]], httpx.Response]]:
+    def post(router: Router, route: str, body: Mapping[str, object]) -> httpx.Response:
+        with TestClient(proxy_server.app) as client:
+            monkeypatch.setattr(proxy_server, "llm_router", router)
+            monkeypatch.setattr(proxy_server, "general_settings", {})
+            monkeypatch.setattr(proxy_server, "prisma_client", None)
+            proxy_server.app.dependency_overrides[user_api_key_auth] = lambda: UserAPIKeyAuth(api_key="hashed-key")
+            return client.post(route, json=body)
+
+    yield post
+    proxy_server.app.dependency_overrides.pop(user_api_key_auth, None)
+
+
+async def _settled(capture: _SuccessCosts) -> None:
+    for _ in range(200):
+        if capture.costs:
+            return
+        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_a_content_policy_fallback_bills_the_filtered_response_with_the_served_one(
+    respx_mock: respx.MockRouter,
+    success_costs: _SuccessCosts,
+    proxy_post: Callable[[Router, str, Mapping[str, object]], httpx.Response],
+) -> None:
+    hits: Final = [0]
+
+    def upstream(_: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
+        hits[0] += 1
+        return httpx.Response(200, json=_chat_body(hits[0], "content_filter" if hits[0] == 1 else "stop"))
+
+    respx_mock.post("https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions").mock(side_effect=upstream)
+    router: Final = Router(
+        model_list=[_deployment("primary", "openai/gpt-4o"), _deployment("backup", "openai/gpt-4o")],
+        content_policy_fallbacks=[{"primary": ["backup"]}],
+    )
+
+    response: Final = await asyncio.to_thread(
+        proxy_post,
+        router,
+        "/v1/chat/completions",
+        {"model": "primary", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]},
+    )

+    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text

+    assert float(response.headers["x-litellm-response-cost"]) == pytest.approx(FIRST_COST + FINAL_COST)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_a_retry_after_a_served_response_bills_both_attempts(
+    respx_mock: respx.MockRouter,
+    success_costs: _SuccessCosts,
+    proxy_post: Callable[[Router, str, Mapping[str, object]], httpx.Response],
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+) -> None:
+    hits: Final = [0]
+
+    def upstream(_: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
+        hits[0] += 1
+        return httpx.Response(200, json=_chat_body(hits[0], "stop"))
+
+    respx_mock.post("https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions").mock(side_effect=upstream)
+    real_acompletion: Final = litellm.acompletion
+
+    async def refused_after_the_first_response(*args: object, **kwargs: object) -> object:  # kwargs-ok: the attempt
+        # The error a provider-side safeguard raises once the first response was served and priced.
+        response: Final = await real_acompletion(*args, **kwargs)
+        if hits[0] == 1:
+            raise litellm.ContentPolicyViolationError(
+                message="refused after the response was served", model="gpt-4o", llm_provider="openai"
+            )
+        return response
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(litellm, "acompletion", refused_after_the_first_response)
+    router: Final = Router(
+        model_list=[_deployment("primary", "openai/gpt-4o")],
+        num_retries=1,
+        retry_policy={"ContentPolicyViolationErrorRetries": 1},
+    )
+
+    response: Final = await asyncio.to_thread(
+        proxy_post,
+        router,
+        "/v1/chat/completions",
+        {"model": "primary", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]},
+    )
+    await _settled(success_costs)
+
+    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
+    assert hits[0] == 2
+    assert response.headers["x-litellm-attempted-retries"] == "1"
+    assert response.json()["usage"]["completion_tokens"] == FINAL_COMPLETION_TOKENS
+    assert success_costs.costs == (pytest.approx(FIRST_COST + FINAL_COST),)
+    assert float(response.headers["x-litellm-response-cost"]) == pytest.approx(FIRST_COST + FINAL_COST)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_a_messages_refusal_fallback_bills_the_refused_response_with_the_served_one(

+) -> None:

+

+    response: Final = await asyncio.to_thread(

+

+    assert hits[0] == 2
+    assert response.json()["usage"]["output_tokens"] == FINAL_COMPLETION_TOKENS
+    assert success_costs.costs == (pytest.approx(FIRST_COST + FINAL_COST),)
+    assert float(response.headers["x-litellm-response-cost"]) == pytest.approx(FIRST_COST + FINAL_COST)

+import httpx
+import pytest
+import respx
+
+import litellm
+from litellm import Router
+from litellm.integrations.custom_logger import CustomLogger
+from litellm.litellm_core_utils.litellm_logging import Logging
+
+INPUT_RATE: Final = 0.001
+OUTPUT_RATE: Final = 0.002
+PROMPT_TOKENS: Final = 10
+MESSAGES: Final = [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]
+PRICING: Final = {"input_cost_per_token": INPUT_RATE, "output_cost_per_token": OUTPUT_RATE}
+
+
+def _cost(attempt: int) -> float:
+    return PROMPT_TOKENS * INPUT_RATE + 10 * attempt * OUTPUT_RATE
+
+
+class _SuccessCosts(CustomLogger):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.costs: tuple[object, ...] = ()
+
+    async def async_log_success_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time) -> None:  # noqa: ANN001  # CustomLogger's untyped hook signature
+        self.costs = (*self.costs, kwargs.get("response_cost"))
+
+
+def _chat_body(attempt: int, finish_reason: str) -> dict[str, object]:  # mutable-ok: a JSON body
+    return {
+        "id": f"chatcmpl-attempt-{attempt}",
+        "object": "chat.completion",
+        "created": 1,
+        "model": "gpt-4o",
+        "choices": [
+            {
+                "index": 0,
+                "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": f"attempt {attempt}"},
+                "finish_reason": finish_reason,
+            }
+        ],
+        "usage": {
+            "prompt_tokens": PROMPT_TOKENS,
+            "completion_tokens": 10 * attempt,
+            "total_tokens": PROMPT_TOKENS + 10 * attempt,
+        },
+    }
+
+
+def _deployment(name: str) -> dict[str, object]:  # mutable-ok: a model_list entry
+    return {
+        "model_name": name,
+        "litellm_params": {"model": "openai/gpt-4o", "api_key": "test-key"},
+        "model_info": PRICING,
+    }
+
+

+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def success_costs(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> _SuccessCosts:

+
+
+async def _logged(capture: _SuccessCosts, count: int) -> None:

+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_a_content_policy_fallback_logs_the_served_response_after_the_filtered_one(
+    respx_mock: respx.MockRouter, success_costs: _SuccessCosts

+    hits: Final = [0]
+
+    def upstream(_: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:

+    )
+

+
+    assert hits[0] == 2

+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio

+

+    respx_mock.post("https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions").mock(side_effect=upstream)
+    real_acompletion: Final = litellm.acompletion
+
+    async def refused_after_the_first_response(*args: object, **kwargs: object) -> object:  # kwargs-ok: the attempt
+        # The error a provider-side safeguard raises once the first response was served and logged.

+    )

+
+class _SyncSuccessLogs(CustomLogger):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.hooked = 0

+
+
+def test_a_sync_content_policy_fallback_logs_both_served_responses_while_the_first_log_is_in_flight(
+    respx_mock: respx.MockRouter, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch

+        model_list=[_deployment("primary"), _deployment("backup")], content_policy_fallbacks=[{"primary": ["backup"]}]
+    )
+

+        model="primary", messages=MESSAGES, litellm_logging_obj=_shared_logging("superseded-sync-fallback")

title: [Bug]: minimax provider silently drops top-level reasoning_effort (M3.1-Flash supports low|medium|high|max)

judge.reasoning: Both patches make the independent tests pass, so the decision rests on root-cause fit, risk, and scope. Patch A fixes the exact cause the issue names: it adds reasoning_effort to MinimaxChatConfig.get_supported_openai_params unconditionally, so the parameter survives drop_params and is forwarded for the provider to judge, matching how the OpenAI-compatible base behaves. Its map_openai_params override is small and defensible (unwraps an {'effort': ...} object to the bare level, skips the 'default' sentinel, and uses the existing warn_dropped_reasoning helper when nothing usable remains), and its tests drive a real litellm.completion through an httpx MockTransport and assert the body carries each of low/medium/high/max. Patch B gates the whitelist on litellm.supports_reasoning, which makes the fix depend on cost-map data: it adds a new MiniMax-M3.1-Flash entry with pricing figures the issue gives no basis for and a reasoning_effort_levels list that includes 'xhigh', contradicting the issue's stated low|medium|high|max set. It then adds a blanket '^minimax/' generalization rule marking every unmapped MiniMax id as reasoning-capable, which is a provider-wide behavior change well beyond the ask. Because litellm normally loads the cost map remotely, B's fix only reaches production once the hosted JSON updates, and in deployments pinned to an older map it would still drop the parameter; A has no such dependency. B's extra tests are thorough but mostly exercise the new cost-map rule and the fabricated entry rather than the reported bug. A resolves the issue at its root with less risk and tighter scope, so A is the better fix.

issue_md:
### What happened

`reasoning_effort` sent at the top level of a Chat Completions request to a MiniMax deployment is silently dropped: it never reaches the upstream and no warning is logged.

- litellm: **1.106.6** (proxy, image `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:latest`)
- deployment: `model_name: minimax-flash` → `litellm_params.model: minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`

### Repro

```bash
curl -s $LITELLM/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"minimax-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"..."}],"max_tokens":1500,"reasoning_effort":"low"}'
curl -s $LITELLM/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"minimax-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"..."}],"max_tokens":1500,"reasoning_effort":"high"}'
```

### Observed

`usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` is the same for `low` and `high` — the parameter is stripped before the upstream call.

Proof the drop is on the litellm side, not MiniMax:

| Request | reasoning_tokens (max_tokens 1500) |
|---|---|
| `extra_body: {"reasoning_effort": "low"}` | 410 |
| `extra_body: {"reasoning_effort": "high"}` | 1499 |
| top-level `reasoning_effort: "low"` / `"high"` | identical (dropped) |
| same deployment as `openai/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` + top-level `reasoning_effort` | low 410 / high 1499 (works) |

### Cause

`litellm/llms/minimax/chat/transformation.py::get_supported_openai_params` only appends `reasoning_split` (and `thinking` when `supports_reasoning`), so `reasoning_effort` is not in the accepted-params set for MiniMax deployment names and gets removed by the drop-params path.

`MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` does accept the effort levels directly — verified against the upstream API, `low|medium|high|max` all work when the parameter is forwarded.

### Related

- #48933 (merged 2026-10-30) added "requested reasoning level was dropped" WARNINGs to the remaining drop sites for `anthropic`, `bedrock`, `azure_ai`, `deepseek`, `fal` — **minimax is still silent**, so callers get no signal at all.
- #47515 attempts to preserve Flash effort levels, but it is currently `mergeable=false` (dirty) and CLA-unsigned since 2026-10-20.

### Ask

Whitelist `reasoning_effort` for the minimax provider so it is forwarded (Flash supports `low|medium|high|max`), or — if that is intentional — emit the same drop WARNING added in #48933 so the silent stripping stops being invisible.
